neighbours.label: a word stating the magnitude of a physical load on a body part or material (excessive stress, greatly increased forces, additional tension, loaded excessively)
fire: Running on concrete puts excessive strain on the ankles and knees.
When the ligament is torn, shear forces across the joint are greatly increased.
The bracket will crack if the bolt is tightened excessively.
A heavy backpack creates additional pressure on the discs of the spine.
Lifting with a rounded back places too much load on the lumbar vertebrae.
If the arch collapses, the stress on the tendon is markedly increased.
The weld failed because the plate had been loaded excessively.
Landing with straight legs sends excessive force through the hip joint.
quiet: Running on concrete is a popular way to train for a city marathon.
When the ligament is torn, most patients see a specialist within a week.
The bracket was painted before the bolt was fitted.
A heavy workload creates additional pressure on the staff of the clinic.
Lifting weights should be done gradually over a period of several months.
If the deadline slips, the stress on the whole team is hard to bear.
The weld was inspected because the plate had been delivered late.
Landing a new job brought excessive excitement to the whole family.

notes: Card: ' stress' x3, ' increased', ' excessively', ' tension', ' range' in biomechanics/materials text. Probes: 'forces … greatly increased' 0.83, 'loaded excessively' 0.58, 'excessive stress on the spine' 0.39, 'additional tension in the cable' 0.32; psychological stress 0.04, 'slowly over a period' 0.02. The − pole fires on rate/duration words (over, quickly, gradual) in the same texts, so the neuron may separate how much load from how fast it is applied.
